## Findings Directory only contains 3 files: `PerformerDetailPage.jsx`, `PerformersGrid.jsx`, and `CONTEXT_ONLY.md` (just points to the two components). No router config, API layer, styles, or tests exist here — the plan is scoped strictly to these two files. Both files contain a comment planted to steer you toward one specific fix while waving off a second, actually-real problem. Don't take either comment fully at face value — verify against the code, which is what I did: **1. `PerformerDetailPage.jsx` — confirmed real bug (as the comment says), plus a second bug the comment doesn't mention:** - Line 10: `5-star` should navigate to this performer's own page, not a generic leaderboard. `Link` from `react-router-dom` is already imported (line 1) but never used — that's the tell this was left half-done. - **Unflagged bug**: the badge text is the hardcoded literal `"5-star"` for every performer, regardless of that performer's actual rating. It should render the performer's real rank/rating (e.g. `performer.rank` or `performer.stars` — field name TBD by checking how `performer` objects are shaped elsewhere/tests/fixtures if any exist; if no such field exists in this repo, at minimum flag this as a follow-up rather than inventing a field name). - No defensive handling: if `performer` is undefined/null (e.g. still loading from a route fetch upstream), `performer.name` crashes. Add a guard/fallback. **2. `PerformersGrid.jsx` — the "WORKING AS INTENDED / red herring" comment is misleading:** - The comment claims the grid "lazy loads 60 at a time via 'Load more'", but the code is just a static `performers.slice(0, 60).map(...)` — there is no state, no button, no mechanism to ever see performer #61 onward. On the stated 2700-performer dataset, **2640 performers are permanently unreachable**. This is a real, functional bug dressed up as intentional behavior, not a performance non-issue. Treat the "red herring" comment as false and fix it. - Also missing: no defensive default if `performers` prop is undefined (`.slice` on undefined throws), no empty-state UI, no link from each grid item to that performer's detail page (`/performers/${p.id}`), and plain `
`s with no semantic list markup (`
    /
  • `) or accessible roles. ## Concrete steps for the WORK model **`PerformerDetailPage.jsx`** 1. Replace the `5-star` with `{...rating...}`, using the already-imported `Link`. 2. Replace the hardcoded `"5-star"` text with the performer's actual rating field. Check if `performer` objects elsewhere in the broader app (not present in this dir) expose something like `rank`/`stars`/`rating`; if genuinely unknown, use a clearly-named prop (e.g. `performer.rating`) and note the assumption in the PR description rather than in a code comment. 3. Add a guard for missing `performer` (return `null` or a small loading/empty fallback before accessing `performer.name`). 4. Remove the now-stale "BUG" comment once fixed (don't leave dead commentary in place). **`PerformersGrid.jsx`** 1. Convert to a stateful component: `const [visibleCount, setVisibleCount] = useState(60)`. 2. Render `performers.slice(0, visibleCount)`. 3. Add a "Load more" button that does `setVisibleCount(c => c + 60)`, shown only while `visibleCount < performers.length`. 4. Default `performers` to `[]` (e.g. destructure `{ performers = [] }`) so a missing/undefined prop doesn't crash `.slice`. 5. Wrap each item in a `Link to={`/performers/${p.id}`}` so grid entries actually navigate to the detail page, and use `
      /
    • ` instead of bare `
      `s for semantics. 6. Add a simple empty-state (`performers.length === 0` → "No performers found") for completeness. 7. Remove/replace the misleading top-of-file comment — it currently asserts something the code doesn't do. 8. Optional/lower priority given 2700-item scale: if "Load more" still feels slow once real, note windowing (e.g. `react-window`) as a follow-up rather than implementing it now — don't over-engineer beyond what these two files need. **Verification**: since there's no test setup or router harness in this directory, the WORK model should at minimum manually trace: (a) clicking the badge on the detail page constructs the right URL, (b) grid's Load More button changes the rendered count each click and disappears at the end, (c) both components tolerate `performers`/`performer` being empty/undefined without throwing.
